_comment: Dispatcher vehicle list and the crew briefing before the arrival on the scene (macro voice approach briefing of the mission, 2 NM from the accident). The mission sends the keys with speak: <say:DSP.VEH.WAY>letters//letters, <say:APR.PLT.G>. The letters are A ambulance, F fire engine, P police; {list:N} writes them as a sentence and {be:N} says is or are. Four options each; option k of the five briefing lines goes together (group approach).

messages.trigger: vehicles dispatched, still on the way (argument 0 = letters)
o: {list:0} {be:0} on the way to the scene.
Be advised, {list:0} {be:0} on the way to the accident.
{list:0} {be:0} en route to your location.
For your information, {list:0} {be:0} on the way.
{list:1} {be:1} already on scene.
Be advised, {list:1} {be:1} already at the accident.
{list:1} {be:1} on location.
For your information, {list:1} {be:1} already on site.

messages.trigger: some vehicles on scene (argument 1), others on the way (argument 0)
o: {list:1} {be:1} already on scene, {list:0} {be:0} on the way.
Be advised, {list:1} {be:1} at the accident and {list:0} {be:0} still on the way.
On location: {list:1}. On the way: {list:0}.
For your information, {list:1} {be:1} on site, {list:0} {be:0} en route.
No rescue vehicles at the location. You will be first on scene.
Be advised, no ground units on scene. The helicopter is first on scene.
No ground units are on the way. You are the first to arrive.
For your information, nobody is on scene yet. You will be first.

messages.trigger: 2 NM from the accident, a landing spot near the patient is expected
o: Approaching the scene. We expect a landing close to the patient, so ground operations.
Almost there. The plan is to land near the patient and work on the ground.
Briefing: we should be able to land close to them. Ground operation.
Two miles out. We aim for a landing near the patient, ground operation.

messages.trigger: 2 NM from the accident, no landing spot near the patient: hoist expected
o: Approaching the scene. There is no good landing area close to the patient, so we plan the hoist.
Almost there. We cannot land close to the patient: the plan is a hoist operation.
Briefing: no landing spot near them. We prepare for the hoist.
Two miles out. No suitable landing near the patient, we expect to hoist.

messages.trigger: police or fire service on scene or on the way
o: Copilot: police or fire service is at the scene. I will ask them for the landing area.
Ground units are there. I will contact them for the landing area and any hazards.
With units on the ground I will coordinate the landing area with them.
Units are on site, I will confirm the landing area and hazards on the radio.
Copilot: no police or fire service there. I check the landing area and the obstacles myself.
Nobody secures the area, so I look for hazards and obstacles while we descend.
No units on the ground, I will scan the area for wires and people.
We are on our own there. I watch obstacles and the surroundings.

messages.trigger: an ambulance on scene or on the way (its crew has no advanced paramedic)
o: Doc: the ambulance crew has no advanced paramedic, so I take the lead on the patient and decide the transport with them.
Doc here. I lead the medical care, the ambulance crew supports and we decide the transport together.
I take over the patient assessment, the ambulance can help and carry out the transport if I agree.
Doc: the ambulance will help, but the medical decisions are mine.
Doc: no ambulance coming, so we treat and stabilize the patient ourselves and plan the transport with the helicopter.
Doc here. Without an ambulance we stabilize and transport the patient ourselves.
No ambulance on the way, I assess and stabilize, then we load the patient.
Doc: we are on our own medically, we stabilize first and decide the transport after.
Rear crew: stretcher and bag ready, I follow Doc on the ground.
Chief: the stretcher is prepared, I go with Doc when we are down.
Rear crew ready for ground operation, stretcher at the door.
Chief here, I carry the stretcher and follow the doctor on the ground.
Rear crew: hoist checked, Doc goes down first, I operate the winch.
Chief: the hoist is ready. The doctor first, I run the cable.
Rear crew ready for hoist, harness and stretcher prepared.
Chief here, hoist set. I operate it, the doctor goes down first.
Good. Everybody stays alert and calls out any obstacle.
Thanks, crew. Eyes outside, call out obstacles and wires.
Alright. Keep your eyes open and tell me what you see.
Understood. Stay focused, we land when the area is clear.
